title: Canonical scalar comparison for rational ordinary cohomology
statement: Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $V=\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=V/\varpi^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $Y$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $f:Y\to s$, and use the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $K$ be an object of $D^b_c(Y,V)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], and write $K_E$ for its image in the rationalized category [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. Use the integral and rational direct images [def-weil-derived-direct-image], the point evaluation of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] and ordinary cohomology of [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology]. For every integer $i$ the canonical cycle-tensor map followed by that point-evaluation comparison is an $E$-linear isomorphism $\tau^i_K:H^i(Y,K)\otimes_V E\xrightarrow{\sim}H^i(Y,K_E)$. If $C^\bullet$ represents the integral point complex, $z\in\ker(d^i:C^i\to C^{i+1})$, and $\lambda\in E$, then $\tau^i_K([z]\otimes\lambda)=[z\otimes\lambda]$ in the rational point complex $C^\bullet\otimes_V E$. The maps are natural in integral coefficient morphisms. For $K=\widehat V_Y$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], a degree-zero class $e$ therefore satisfies $\tau^0_K(e\otimes1)=[e\otimes1]$; when $e$ is the integral unit class, this is the rational unit class specified by rational point evaluation. There is no connectedness, properness, smoothness, or prior computation of $H^0(Y,K)$ among the hypotheses.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-integral-direct-image-constructible] to $f:Y\to s$ over $k$: both schemes are finite type over $k$ and $\ell$ is invertible since $\ell\ne p$. Thus $L=Rf_*K$ lies in $D^b_c(s,V)$. Choose an algebraic closure of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ containing $E$, as permitted in the coefficient conventions. The strict direct image is $V$-linear by [lem-sf-strict-direct-image-scalar-comparison], applied to the same separated finite-type morphism. Its rationalization therefore sends an integral morphism $u$ to $Rf_*(u)\otimes1$, with the same object $L$, by [def-weil-derived-direct-image, def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. Choose any module complex $C^\bullet$ representing $\operatorname{Fib}_s L$. By [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] (2)-(3) the rational point complex is represented by $C^\bullet\otimes_V E$, with integral morphisms extended termwise. Hence [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology] identifies the two cohomology groups in the assertion with $H^i(C^\bullet)$ and $H^i(C^\bullet\otimes_V E)$.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr] (1), $E$ is the fraction field of the domain $V$. For $T=V\setminus\{0\}$, the inclusion $V\to E$ satisfies the three localization conditions of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat]: nonzero denominators become units, every field element is a fraction, and an element of $V$ mapping to zero already vanishes. That node gives flatness of $E$ over $V$. Consequently [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] applies to every exact sequence of $V$-modules below.

Write $Z^i=\ker d^i$, $B^i=\operatorname{im}d^{i-1}$. Tensor the sequences $0\to Z^i\to C^i\to B^{i+1}\to0$, $0\to B^{i+1}\to C^{i+1}$ and $0\to B^i\to Z^i\to H^i(C^\bullet)\to0$. They stay exact by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] (including surjectivity by applying it to the last three terms ending in zero). The differential after tensoring factors through the surjection onto $B^{i+1}\otimes_V E$ and its injection into $C^{i+1}\otimes_V E$. Thus its kernel is $Z^i\otimes_V E$, and its boundaries are $B^i\otimes_V E$ inside that kernel. The third sequence identifies their quotient with $H^i(C^\bullet)\otimes_V E$. The induced inverse quotient identification is $[z]\otimes\lambda\mapsto[z\otimes\lambda]$: replacing $z$ by $z+d w$ changes the image by $d(w\otimes\lambda)$. This is the specified canonical map, and it is $E$-linear because multiplication acts on the second tensor factor.

For a chain map $h:C^\bullet\to D^\bullet$, the two naturality composites send $[z]\otimes\lambda$ to $[h(z)\otimes\lambda]$; pure tensors generate, so the composites agree. The isomorphism in Step 3 implies that tensoring any quasi-isomorphism is again a quasi-isomorphism. By the localization definition [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], this naturality identity passes to derived morphisms: it holds for chain maps, therefore for inverses of quasi-isomorphisms, and hence for all composites generating the localization. It also shows independence of the representing complex. Combine with the functorial point identifications in Step 1 to obtain the required maps $\tau^i_K$ and their naturality in integral coefficient morphisms.

proof.text: For $K=\widehat V_Y$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], insert $i=0$ and $\lambda=1$ in Step 3 to obtain $\tau^0_K(e\otimes1)=[e\otimes1]$. In particular the integral unit class is represented by the coefficient section $1$; its rational point-evaluation class is, by item (3) of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], the class of that same section tensored with $1$. This proves the unit normalization without computing the group $H^0(Y,K)$ or assuming connectedness, properness or smoothness.
